title: Gradient reserve crediting pilot - variable-duration reserved GPUs with autoscale buffers
creator: Sofia Patel
description: Problem: Large customers need predictable committed spend for dedicated GPU capacity while retaining burst/elasticity for traffic spikes. Current commit and burst models are either too rigid (fixed-month reservations) or too permissive (pay-as-you-go burst that hurts unit economics for Redwood). Objective: Run a pilot that tests a 'gradient reserve crediting' model in which customers commit to multi-duration reservation bands (short, medium, long) and receive graduated reservoir credits that soften burst usage, paired with an autoscale buffer that can borrow from a shared pool. The pilot should produce contractual language for enterprise SQs, legal terms for burst-credit reconciliation, and a recommended pricing ladder for GA.
acceptance_criteria: Run cohort experiment with >= 10 enterprise pilot customers representing at least 3 industries
Define 3 reservation bands (4-week, 3-month, 12-month) and associated credit taper curves
Measure per-token unit cost delta vs baseline (current reserved + burst) and show >= 8% cost improvement for typical batch workloads
Produce contract appendix language (SLA bands, burst-credit accounting, preemption rules) cleared by legal and sales
Consolidate security questionnaire responses for pilot customers (SAML, KMS, SOC2 scope) and surface any blockers
success_metrics: Pilot conversion rate to paid commitment >= 30% within 90 days
Average monthly committed GPU hours sold per pilot >= 250 GPU-hours
0sev production incidents attributable to autoscale borrow pool during pilot
Net revenue uplift vs control group >= 12% after adjusting for discounting
rollout_plan: Phase A (4 weeks): Internal engineering simulation and pricing model calibration using historical tenancy traces (eng-runbook link)
Phase B (6 weeks): Invite 10 pilot customers, deploy pilot pricing via dedicated UI flag (console feature flag), monitor dashboards
Phase C (4 weeks): Iterate pricing curves and contract language based on telemetry and customer feedback
Phase D (GA prep): Finalize product SKU taxonomy, billing reconciliation flows, and legal playbook for renewals
decisions: Use three bands rather than continuous negotiation for easier sales motion and simpler billing reconciliation
Autoscale buffer will be implemented as a shared borrow pool with tenant caps (soft cap then throttling), not per-tenant unlimited burst
Burst credits will taper linearly by default but allow negotiated non-linear taper curves for strategic accounts
tradeoffs: Simplicity vs competitiveness: More bands simplify ops but may leave money on the table for high-variance workloads
Risk of abuse: Shared borrow pool reduces per-tenant isolation guarantees — mitigated by caps and preemption rules
Billing complexity: Graduated credits complicate invoice explanations — requires clear console visualizations and line-item export
